These are judgment-based estimates. I did not compute them from the benchmark tables.

| Claim | Prob. | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 30 | Alpha only matters near its top values, and there is no strong reason it should depend on width. |
| 1 | 35 | Deep, wide nets may be less stable at high learning rates, but the effect is weak. |
| 2 | 45 | Heavy L2 combined with more layers plausibly underfits more, so removing a layer could help. |
| 3 | 35 | No clear mechanism. |
| 4 | 30 | No clear mechanism. |
| 5 | 35 | No clear mechanism. |
| 6 | 30 | Wide nets probably diverge sooner at high learning rates, which would make the effect lower. |
| 7 | 60 | If the L2 penalty is scaled per minibatch (as in sklearn), large batches weaken it, so raising alpha hurts less. |
| 8 | 40 | No clear mechanism. |
| 9 | 35 | No clear mechanism. |
| 10 | 35 | No clear mechanism. |
| 11 | 40 | Small, noisy batches may destabilize deeper nets. |
| 12 | 55 | At high learning rates training is often already broken, so alpha matters less there and its usual harm is muted. |
| 13 | 35 | No clear mechanism. |
| 14 | 55 | Narrow deep nets do worse, so dropping a layer helps more when width is low. |
| 15 | 30 | The biggest gain from a smaller batch should come at the large end, where there are few update steps. |
| 16 | 35 | No clear mechanism. |
| 17 | 15 | At low learning rates, a larger batch means fewer steps and more underfitting, so the effect is lower. |
| 18 | 25 | Large batches tolerate higher learning rates, so lowering the learning rate helps less. |
| 19 | 35 | No clear mechanism. |
| 20 | 40 | No clear mechanism. |
| 21 | 35 | No clear mechanism. |
| 22 | 35 | No clear mechanism. |
| 23 | 60 | Shrinking an already wide net costs little, while shrinking a narrow one costs more. |
| 24 | 45 | Compares 3→2 layers against 2→1 layers. |
| 25 | 35 | No clear mechanism. |
| 26 | 20 | With small batches, raising the learning rate is more likely to cause instability. |
| 27 | 8 | Lowering an already low learning rate causes underfitting, while lowering a high one helps, so the effect is clearly lower. |
